ADMISSION CONSULTATION

Reason for consultation: GI bleeding on anticoagulation.

History: 71-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation on apixaban who presents with coffee-ground emesis x3 and melenic stool overnight. Epigastric discomfort, no severe pain. No NSAIDs, no alcohol. Took apixaban this morning. No prior GI bleed.

Past history: Atrial fibrillation, hypertension, GERD.

Current meds: Apixaban 5 mg BID; Metoprolol 50 mg BID; Omeprazole 20 mg daily.

Social: Lives with husband. No tobacco, no alcohol.

Examination: Vitals T 98.1 F, HR 108, BP 102/64, RR 18, SpO2 96% RA. Pale, alert. Abdomen soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Rectal: melenic stool, heme positive.

Laboratory: Hgb 8.4 (L), BUN 32, Creatinine 1.0, INR 1.4.

Electrocardiogram: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, rate 104.

Impression: 71-year-old anticoagulated woman with acute upper GI bleed.

Recommendations:
1. Upper GI bleed on apixaban — hold apixaban, GI consult for urgent endoscopy, type and cross, IV PPI.
2. Atrial fibrillation — continue metoprolol for rate control, telemetry, reassess stroke risk off anticoagulation.
